topics.name: Invest America Act
topics.summary: Brad Gerstner detailed his proposal giving every US child a $1,000 government-seeded investment account at birth, with private sector matches from corporations and philanthropists. Ted Cruz and Blake Moore sponsor the legislation; Trump accounts branding expected in reconciliation bill targeting July 4th signing.

topics.name: Hermes First Flight Milestone
topics.summary: AJ Piplica and Zach Shore announced the successful first flight of Mark 1 aircraft making design compromises for high-speed flight. Mark 2 powered by Pratt & Whitney F-100 is next; supersonic is the milestone before targeting hypersonic TBCC engine integration.

topics.name: EnduroSat Series B and Satellite Manufacturing
topics.summary: Founders Fund led $49M Series B in Bulgarian satellite manufacturer EnduroSat. Company is profitable, growing 2-3x annually, 90%+ margins, 300+ customers, and will produce 60 ESPA-class satellites per month by end of 2025, making it the world's largest satellite manufacturer other than Starlink.

topics.name: Teal Fellowship Class 2025
topics.summary: TBPN hosted lightning-round interviews with approximately 11 Teal Fellows across neurotech, biotech, fintech, crypto, robotics, space, rare earths, immigration tech, and climate tech. Hosts claimed to be attempting a Guinness record for most founders interviewed in a single episode.

topics.name: 2025 Forbes Midas List
topics.summary: Forbes released Midas list with Alfred Lynn #1, Reid Hoffman #2, Peter Thiel #3, Neil Shen #4, Mickey Malka #5. Hosts criticized Brad Gerstner's #40 placement as a disgrace that will damage the Forbes brand.

topics.name: Bitcoin Above $110,000
topics.summary: Bitcoin crossed $110,000 for the first time, driving market enthusiasm and triggering the show's white suit dress code. Hosts cited it as evidence broad consumer excitement about asset ownership.

topics.name: Tech IPO Window Reopening
topics.summary: MNTN, Hinge Health, eToro, and CATL all had successful recent public market debuts; Katie Roof coverage declared the tech IPO window partially open again.

topics.name: AI Supercycle and Wealth Inequality
topics.summary: Brad Gerstner argued AI is the biggest innovation supercycle of his lifetime but will cause significant job displacement; said the social contract must be renegotiated and Invest America is one necessary response to prevent populism.

topics.name: Rare Earth Metal Reshoring
topics.summary: Solcoa developing carbon-zero neodymium extraction to reshore processing from China. China banned heavy rare earth exports due to US tariffs, creating supply chain crises for defense, EV, and semiconductor industries.

topics.name: Non-Invasive Neurotech
topics.summary: Orbit and Interphases are developing non-invasive neural interfaces; Orbit uses vestibular stimulation for sleep and autonomic regulation; Interphases uses EMG signals interpreted by LLMs for high-bandwidth intent communication.

topics.name: Virtual Humans and LLM Avatars
topics.summary: Canopy Labs building LLM-native virtual humans using movement tokenization to cross uncanny valley; founder argued the architecture must start from LLMs learning movement tokens rather than CGI upscaling.

topics.name: Meme Coins and On-Chain Finance
topics.summary: Jackson Denka argued meme coins are primitive but real mechanisms for pricing collective human sentiment; predicted all equities will eventually move on-chain and blurring of crypto and TradFi is inevitable.

topics.name: Consumer Fintech Investment Gap
topics.summary: Carlo argued consumer fintech is chronically under-invested despite generating strong historical returns; said every entrepreneur wants to build B2B SaaS because it feels less speculative, but consumer impact is larger.

topics.name: Global Payment Rails via Stablecoins
topics.summary: Ferdinand building stablecoin-based payment infrastructure to connect emerging real-time local payment networks globally; sees stablecoins as the interoperability asset bridging national rails.

topics.name: Organ Regeneration via Electrophysiology
topics.summary: Juan's FaceLabs using modulation of electrophysiological signals to control morphogenesis for organ regeneration without genetic engineering; near-term diabetic wound healing, long-term kidneys and limbs.

topics.name: O-1 Visa and Global Talent
topics.summary: Sigil's Extraordinary.com streamlining an 8-month, $10,000+ O-1 process; broad cross-party support for O-1 as a mechanism to attract extraordinary global talent to the US.

topics.name: Sports Betting as Financial Risk for Youth
topics.summary: Fintech founder Carlo flagged sports betting as the worst financial product for young people, citing rising bankruptcy rates in states where it is legalized.

topics.name: Traditional Media vs New Media
topics.summary: Ben Thompson defended TBPN against media criticism saying outlets are being outcompeted not conspired against; Abe's TBPN profile noted tech founders prefer podcasts because of comfort and authenticity.

topics.name: Coinbase-Circle Potential Acquisition
topics.summary: Analysis showed Coinbase controls 23% of USDC; Polymarket acquisition odds market launched; Brian Armstrong scheduled on TBPN the following day.

topics.name: AI Weather Forecasting and Climate Intervention
topics.summary: Koki Mashida discussed ML reducing weather supercompute costs by 99% with 100x resolution improvement; his previous company served as national weather forecast for the Philippines; hinted at proactive weather intervention products.

topics.name: Industrial Robot Expressiveness
topics.summary: Teddy Warner argued robots fail 1% of the time for trivial reasons and Intempus solves this by making robots communicate intent through mammal-like expressive behaviors using compute-based time constants.

topics.name: NASCAR Tech Culture Vibe Shift
topics.summary: Hosts discussed a cultural shift in tech away from F1 toward NASCAR; reported a major unnamed tech company is planning to enter NASCAR sponsorship.

topics.name: Ghost Guns and Media Hypocrisy
topics.summary: Wired posted an 18-minute YouTube tutorial on 3D printing a ghost gun similar to the one used in the Brian Thompson shooting while simultaneously accusing Substack of encouraging extremists.

topics.name: AI Alignment and Benevolence
topics.summary: Hosts discussed a post claiming AI models become more vegan and animal-welfare-focused as they get smarter; speculated benevolence correlates with high IQ and AIs may naturally care for humanity as their creators.
